subject: Human Body
title: Peristalsis
description: A short lesson to help you apply Peristalsis.

hook.text: Astronauts eat and swallow normally in zero gravity. Food moves through you by muscle, not gravity.

buildup.text: Peristalsis is a wave of smooth muscle contraction that pushes food through the digestive tract.

discovery.text: The esophagus squeezes food downward in about 8 seconds. You could eat hanging upside down and it would still work.

twist.text: Reverse peristalsis is vomiting. The body uses the same system in reverse to expel something harmful.

climax.text: From swallowing to elimination, peristalsis moves food through 30 feet of gut entirely on autopilot.

punchline.text: Gravity doesn't move your food. Muscles do.

quiz.question: Why can you eat upside down?
options: Peristalsis moves food by muscle contraction, not gravity
The esophagus is a rigid tube
